own_solution.law: Kinetic theory of an ideal gas: v_rms = sqrt(3 R T / M) = sqrt(3 * 8.314 * 300 / 0.004) = sqrt(1.87065e6) = 1367.7 m/s
assumptions: ideal gas in thermal equilibrium (Maxwell-Boltzmann distribution)

defect_reasons.other: TB33A is in the past tense ('A heater warmed this gas sample by 100 K before its molecular speeds were measured') while the problem says the gas 'is' at 300 K, so it can also be read as the 300 K being the temperature after heating (answer 1367.7 m/s) rather than before (1579.3 m/s); TC501 is clearer.

notes: Base: 3RT/M = 3*8.314*300/0.004 = 1.87065e6 m^2/s^2, v_rms = 1367.7 m/s. With T = 400 K: 2.4942e6, v_rms = 1579.3 m/s. Amount of gas (T181D, TAE95, both 2 mol, wording-only variants): n enters e.g. v_rms = sqrt(3pV/(nM)) via pV = nRT, but cancels, so C. Heating of the other flask (TA59B, T5266) is D: separate flask, no thermal contact stated. Earlier-experiment heating (T5F7E, T9888) is D: gas is now stated to be in equilibrium at 300 K. Number check: TA59B and T5F7E say 'a few kelvin' while T5266, T9888, TB33A, TC501 say '100 K'; if the 'few kelvin' sentences are claimed as same-number variants of 100 K sentences they are not. Clarity is otherwise good; my medium flag concerns the TB33A temporal reading.
